stem: A 500 N crate sits on a level floor with a static friction coefficient of 0.35. A rope pulls on it at 30° above the horizontal. What rope force starts the crate moving?
eli5: The upward component of the rope force reduces the normal force, which reduces the friction available. Write equilibrium in both directions at impending motion: horizontal pull = coefficient × (weight minus vertical pull).
solution:
Normal force: N = 500 - P sin 30°.

Impending motion: P cos 30° = 0.35(500 - P sin 30°).

P = \frac{0.35(500)}{cos 30° + 0.35 sin 30°} = \frac{175}{1.041} = 168.1 N.

stem: A 200 N force acts along a line that rises 7 units for every 24 units of horizontal run. What is its horizontal component?
eli5: When a direction is given as a slope, the components are the force times the side ratios of the slope triangle. The hypotenuse is the square root of rise squared plus run squared.
solution:
Hypotenuse = \sqrt{7^{2} + 24^{2}} = 25.

F_{x} = 200 × \frac{24}{25} = 192.0 N. The vertical component is 200 × \frac{7}{25} = 56.0 N.
